clue.text: Ape hides article in top branches

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so the ape synonym holds the article

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A monkey conceals some item up among the treetops.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopy is the uppermost layer of foliage in a forest, formed by the top branches.

clue.text: People loved abandoning Deacon motors briskly

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so these letters drop out of the clue's two words

parts.note: the letters left after the deletion happen also to run unbroken in these two words, a coincidence of the setter's deletion device
loved people are dears

explanation.surface: Fans walk away from a car dealer called Deacon Motors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes D, E, A, R and S, in that order but scattered, out of DEACON MOTORS, leaving the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Con moto is an Italian musical direction meaning with movement, played briskly.

clue.text: Greek island's vulgar footwear one turned up

definitions.note: the 's here stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: sox is a cheap, informal spelling of socks
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: Someone on a Greek island sports tacky socks upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Naxos is the largest island of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Rough heavy metal bar in Tamworth club?

parts.note: the Tamworth is a British breed of pig, hence the question mark
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Some crude metal ingot is found in a club in the town of Tamworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a Staffordshire town but also a ginger breed of pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is crude iron cast in bars straight from the blast furnace, rough and heavy.

clue.text: Spent penny once, going to London, following custom

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the custom synonym leads

parts.note: use is custom or habit, as in usage
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny before 1971
one goes up to London, the capital, in British idiom

explanation.surface: A Victorian spends a penny on the way to the capital, as was customary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent penny' recalls the euphemism for visiting the lavatory; 'Spent' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used up is spent, exhausted or consumed.

clue.text: See 8
Date next to sheets with tender gorgeous hunk

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper sheets, 500 of them
a tender is a small boat serving a larger ship

explanation.surface: A romantic date between the sheets with a tender, handsome man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is slang for a very attractive man, a heart-throb.

clue.text: Clown's depression — without sin nothing

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the depression goes around the rest

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
to err is to sin or go astray
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A clown's gloom: no sin, nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the white-faced sad clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: A standard self-observation you might make on the verge of solving this clue?

definitions.text: A standard self-observation you might make on the verge of solving this clue?

parts.words: A standard self-observation you might make on the verge of solving this clue?
parts.note: the familiar remark of someone just starting to understand, and also the title of a jazz standard

explanation.surface: A solver mutters a well-known line when nearly cracking this very clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' points to the jazz song by Duke Ellington, while the phrase is also what a dawning solver says.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock expression for gradually understanding, and a famous Ellington standard.

clue.text: See 15
Boring-looking like an eagle?

definitions.meaning: a gimlet is a boring tool, so a piercing look has a gimlet's boring quality
eagles are famed for keen, sharp sight

explanation.definitionFit: Gimlet-eyed means having a piercing, sharp-sighted stare, the eagle's proverbial keenness.

clue.text: Catching cat impetigo finally impregnates dreamer

indicators.note: impregnates means fills or enters, so the final letter goes inside

parts.note: a muser is someone lost in thought, a dreamer

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of impetigo

explanation.surface: A cat with a skin infection passes it on to a daydreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat valued for catching mice.

clue.text: Here, Pam's bust injected with last of silicone — it won't last

indicators.note: injected with means something goes inside the scrambled letters
bust means broken, so the letters of here and Pam are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of silicone

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgery jibe: Pam's chest has had silicone put in, and it won't last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like the body part but signals the anagram of HEREPAM; 'injected with' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are short-lived things, items that won't last beyond a day or so.

clue.text: Adrift, mid ocean, without soft puzzle collections

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the soft letter
adrift means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Drifting mid-ocean without anything soft, someone does a book of puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adrift' rearranges MIDOCEAN, and 'without' places that around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are collected volumes, here of puzzles.

clue.text: Parking upset Montreal traffic police

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of Montreal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Parking chaos has upset Montreal's traffic officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrolmen are police officers on a beat, here dealing with traffic.

clue.text: Military post reportedly battled against criticisms

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: battled means fought, and criticisms are knocks, so the phrase reads fought knocks

explanation.surface: Word is that the army base fought off its critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Knox is a US Army post in Kentucky, home of the gold depository.

clue.text: See 25
Ray embraces North, the philosopher

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the ray synonym goes around the rest

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light
th' is the dialect form of the, in northern English speech

explanation.surface: A beam of light reaches north to the thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: TH for 'the' is the clipped northern English th'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism.

clue.text: Enjoying the delights of Nancy, for example — at Nancy's expense?

definitions.text: Enjoying the delights of Nancy, for example
definitions.meaning: out for a night's entertainment in a town such as Nancy in France
paid for by the municipality, here Nancy

explanation.definitionFit: Being out for the evening's pleasures, or having something paid for by the municipality.

clue.text: Spot difference in hero Ben, a rash type

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the hero's surname

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the hero of Lew Wallace's novel and the famous film

indicators.note: difference suggests change, so the letters of spot are altered

explanation.surface: Spot the difference in the hero Ben, a reckless sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot difference' poses as the children's picture puzzle; the hero is Ben-Hur, of the Lew Wallace novel and Charlton Heston film.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotspur, nickname of Harry Percy, is a byword for a hot-headed, impetuous person.

clue.text: Rogue with Ron Shooter

parts.note: Ron as written
a gun is a shooter

explanation.surface: A villain teams up with Ron the gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong 'un is British slang for a dishonest person, a rogue.

clue.text: Threaten to get out of denim pants initially

indicators.note: out of here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of pants

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to strip off their denim trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges DENIM with P, the first letter of 'pants'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over, as a threat does.

clue.text: "Heart of Juno" by Green is rare

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: a common is a village green

explanation.surface: A quotation, Heart of Juno, by an author named Green is hard to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon is unusual, rare.

clue.text: Candlemaker's big expression of pain

definitions.note: the definition means the candlemaker's material, a noun

parts.note: tall means big in height
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A candlemaker gives a huge yelp of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow, rendered animal fat, was the traditional material of candles.

clue.text: See 8
Impotency, Henry, turned smoker's head

indicators.note: turned means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry's impotence turned out to be a smoker's problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' looks like a person with cigarettes but is a house's chimney; the top is its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimney top is the head of a chimney, the house's smoker.

clue.text: Lots of storage space for carriage with a punch, it's said

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage

indicators.note: it's said means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: bite is punch, sharpness or zest

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn trap with plenty of zing, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigabyte is a large unit of computer storage, a billion bytes.

clue.text: One quarter into gloomy, mournful song by soloist

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the quarter goes inside the gloomy word

parts.note: moody means gloomy or sullen
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A dash of gloom pervades a sad solo song.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is an ode or lament sung by one voice, a solo elegy.

clue.text: Surrealist native of NW France

definitions.meaning: someone from Brittany in north-west France

explanation.definitionFit: André Breton founded Surrealism; a native of Brittany shares that word as name.
